@story A Rainy Saturday
On Saturday the [weather] was terrible. I forgot my [umbrella], so I got very wet. I went to the [library] to read, but it was not [quiet] because a baby was crying. After two hours I was [tired], so I went home and made soup in the [kitchen].
extra: expensive, journey

@story My Neighbour's Dog
My [neighbour] has a big, friendly dog called Max. Max is never [angry]; he just wants to play. One day I wanted to [borrow] a ladder, so I knocked on the door. Max jumped on me and ate my [breakfast] sandwich! The road outside is [dangerous], so we always walk him in the park. Next time I must [remember] to hide my food!
extra: cheap, busy

## Unit 12 · People and places
level C1
text en
id demo-c1-u12

erratic | adj | Unpredictable, inconsistent, irregular
  > His [erratic] dance moves changed every second, so even the DJ couldn't keep up. | eloquent, lavish, adept
  >> His [erratic] driving frightened everyone in the car.
  ! predictable
  = unpredictable
  ~ fluctuate
  ? erratik, eratic
  * 1
secluded | adj | Hard to reach, hidden away
  > The WiFi was so bad in the [secluded] cabin that they made friends with the squirrels. | eloquent, adept, colloquial
  >> The cabin was so [secluded] that the WiFi never worked.
  ! accessible
  = hidden
  ? secludded, sekluded
  * 1
fluctuate | v | To rise and fall irregularly
  > His mood seems to [fluctuate] like the stock market: happy with pizza, gloomy without it. | admonish, coerce, alienate
  ! stabilize
  ? flucuate, fluctuete
  * 2
admonish | v | To warn or scold someone
  > The teacher had to [admonish] the cat for knocking over the vase. | fluctuate, alienate, flourish
  ! praise
  = scold
  ? admonnish, admonesh
  * 3
colloquial | adj | Used in casual conversation
  > His speech was so full of [colloquial] slang that even his grandma was confused. | secluded, ephemeral, adept
  ! formal
  = casual
  ? colloquel, coloquial
  * 3

  > Talking only about traffic lights can quickly [alienate] your friends. | admonish, fluctuate, coerce
  ! befriend
  = isolate
  ? alianate, alienete

  ! inept

  ? adeptt, adpet

  > He tried to [coerce] his little brother into trading chocolate for a carrot. | fluctuate, admonish, alienate
  ! persuade gently

  >> It was [inevitable] that he would trip while texting.

@group Short-lived: ephemeral, transient, fleeting, momentary
@group Found everywhere: ubiquitous, pervasive, omnipresent, universal
@group Unpredictable: erratic, capricious, mercurial, volatile
@group Criticise someone: admonish, reproach, chide, berate
@group Praise someone: exalt, extol, laud, commend
@group Make someone do something: coerce, compel, cajole, induce
@scale How angry?: irritated (a little annoyed) < angry (clearly upset) < furious (extremely angry)
@scale How happy?: content (quietly satisfied) < happy (pleased) < elated (very happy and excited) < ecstatic (overwhelmed with joy)
@scale How afraid?: uneasy (slightly worried) < anxious (nervous about what may happen) < frightened (afraid) < terrified (extremely afraid)
@scale How important?: trivial (hardly matters) < minor (small in importance) < significant (important) < momentous (hugely important, historic)
@scale How big?: small (not big) < large (big) < huge (very big) < gargantuan (enormous, giant)
@sort Positive or negative?: Positive = frugal (careful with money, sensibly), thrifty (good at saving money), confident (sure of yourself), assertive (states views firmly and respectfully), curious (eager to learn), determined (keeps going toward a goal) | Negative = stingy (unwilling to spend or share), miserly (hates spending, even when it is needed), arrogant (thinks they are better than others), aggressive (ready to attack or argue), nosy (too interested in other people's business), stubborn (refuses to change, even when wrong)
@sort Too much, too little, or enough?: Too much = glut (far more supply than is needed), surfeit (an excessive amount), plethora (a very large, often too large, amount), excess (more than is allowed or needed) | Too little = paucity (a scarcity of something), dearth (a lack of something), scarcity (not enough to meet demand), shortage (less than is needed) | Enough = adequate (good enough for the need), sufficient (as much as is needed), satisfactory (acceptable, meets the standard), enough (as much as needed)
@parts biology = bio- (life) + -logy (study of) | The study of living things
@parts telescope = tele- (far) + scope (look, see) | An instrument for seeing things far away
@parts autograph = auto- (self) + graph (write) | A signature you write yourself
@parts transport = trans- (across) + port (carry) | To carry from one place across to another
@parts interrupt = inter- (between) + rupt (break) | To break in while someone is speaking
@parts predict = pre- (before) + dict (say) | To say what will happen before it does
@parts visible = vis (see) + -ible (able to be) | Able to be seen
@parts incredible = in- (not) + cred (believe) + -ible (able to be) | So surprising it is hard to believe
@parts dismiss = dis- (away) + miss (send) | To send someone away
@parts subway = sub- (under) + way (path) | A railway that runs under the ground

@story The Birthday Magician
Max planned a [lavish] party, with a chocolate fountain and three bands. His friends were [skeptical] that a real magician would come. When the magician arrived, his act was [erratic]: one trick was brilliant, the next a disaster. After the rabbit escaped, chaos was [inevitable]. Max's dad stepped in to [admonish] the magician, but the magician gave such an [eloquent] apology that everyone clapped.
extra: ephemeral, secluded

@story Aunt Lola's Cabin
Aunt Lola moved to a [secluded] cabin at the end of a forest road. Phones may be [ubiquitous] in the city, but out there nobody had one. Her love of silence was far from [ephemeral]: it lasted thirty years. She became [adept] at fixing everything herself, from roofs to radios. Her nephew tried to [coerce] her into buying a phone, but she simply laughed and said it would be [detrimental] to her peace.
extra: lavish, colloquial
